title: Drill: Which Server Gets the Mail?

questions.prompt: `MX 10 mx1.shop.example.` and `MX 20 mx2.shop.example.` Both are up. Where does the mail go?
Same records, but mx1 refuses the connection. What next?
`MX 10 a.example.net`, `MX 10 b.example.net`, `MX 10 c.example.net`. How is mail spread?
options: Roughly evenly, since senders pick at random among equal priorities
In alphabetical order, one per day

questions.prompt: A domain has `MX 0 mail.example.org` and `MX 100 backup.example.org`. Which host name gets mail normally? (the full name)
Changing priorities from 10 and 20 to 1 and 2 changes which server is tried first.
A domain has no MX records and no A record. What happens to mail sent there?
options: It goes to the TLD's servers
It bounces: there's nowhere to deliver it

questions.prompt: A domain has no MX but its name has an A record of 203.0.113.9. What does the sender do?
options: Connects to 203.0.113.9 port 25, treating it as an implicit MX

questions.prompt: You want to publish that `noreply.example.com` never accepts mail. What goes after `MX 0`? (one character)
An MX record's value can be an IP address, like `MX 10 192.0.2.25`.
